title: Risk-Controlled Early Exit for Diffusion Language Models

contributions.purpose: Provide formal, distribution-free quality guarantees for early exit in diffusion language models, replacing heuristically tuned fixed thresholds.
contributions.mechanism: RC-Jot, a calibration framework that wraps around existing early exit methods (Jot) and applies conformal risk control with UCB-HB bounds to select the least conservative threshold satisfying a user-specified risk constraint.
contributions.evaluation: Presented as the first application of conformal risk control to DLLM early exit, with high-probability control at level 1-delta.
contributions.source_quote: We present the first application of conformal risk control to early exit in diffusion language models, providing distribution-free guarantees on accuracy degradation.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate that risk-controlled threshold selection preserves speedup while keeping accuracy degradation within budget.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical evaluation of RC-Jot's selected thresholds against risk budgets on math and code benchmarks.
contributions.evaluation: 0% violation rate on GSM8K with 1.36x speedup at epsilon=0.10, and <=1% violation on HumanEval with 1.32x speedup at epsilon=0.15, versus 52% violation for naive threshold selection.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate empirically that RC-Jot achieves 0% violation rate on GSM8K with 1.36x speedup at epsilon = 0.10, and <=1% violation on HumanEval with 1.32x speedup at epsilon = 0.15.

contributions.purpose: Identify which calibration method best trades off guarantee strength against speedup.
contributions.mechanism: Comparison of three calibration methods (Naive, CRC, UCB-HB) within the RC-Jot framework.
contributions.evaluation: UCB-HB provides the best balance between guarantee strength and speedup, particularly with small calibration sets.
contributions.source_quote: We compare calibration methods (Naive, CRC, UCB-HB) and show that UCB-HB provides the best balance between guarantee strength and speedup, particularly with small calibration sets.

contributions.purpose: Give practitioners guidance on how to design the threshold grid for calibration.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation over threshold grid granularity in the RC-Jot calibration procedure.
contributions.evaluation: Medium-granularity grids (15-20 values) are sufficient for effective calibration while coarse grids can cause complete speedup loss.
contributions.source_quote: We provide practical guidance on threshold grid design, showing that medium-granularity grids (15-20 values) are sufficient while coarse grids can cause complete speedup loss.

self_declared_provenance.quote: RC-Jot applies conformal risk control (Angelopoulos et al., 2025) to the early exit setting, using held-out calibration data to select the least conservative threshold that satisfies the risk bound.

Most relevant to our work, Fast-yet-Safe (Jazbec et al., 2024) applies risk control to early exit in autoregressive models, demonstrating that distribution-free guarantees can enable safe acceleration. Our work extends this paradigm to diffusion language models, addressing the distinct challenge of step-wise rather than layer-wise early exit.

notes: Method section (page 2) additionally states RC-Jot 'wraps around Jot (Kohut et al., 2026), a token-level early stopping method', making the wrapper relationship to prior work explicit. Contribution list has 4 bullets; C2-C4 are empirical/guidance findings rather than new methods.
